summary: Joseph Campbell worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Dartmouth, Columbia under William Witherle Lawrence, Paris, and Munich. He served at Columbia (1927), Canterbury School (1933), and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at McGill University, where he studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and Wisconsin under Richard Hartshorne. He taught at Pennsylvania (1960), Jawaharlal Nehru University (1979–1980), and Minnesota (1964–2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at University College School and the University of London, he served at Harris Manchester College, Oxford as President (ca. 1876–1915) and at the University of Oxford (ca. 1889–1915).

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Columbia and under teachers including Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (1989).

Joseph Hackin worked in archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sciences Po, INALCO, EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, and Paris. He held posts at Musée Guimet, EPHE, École du Louvre, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and DAFA.

Joseph Haroutunian was a religious studies scholar educated at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University, and Union Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Wellesley College (1932–1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Rikkyo, CDSP, Bexley Seabury, and Chicago under Joachim Wach. He spent his career at Chicago (1951–1987), including as Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College and Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He was a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).
Joseph Margolis was a philosophy scholar who earned his M.A. at Columbia University (ca. 1947–1950). He served as the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University (1991).

Joseph A. Marino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, later serving there as Assistant Professor (attested 2026).

Joseph Needham worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle School, Gonville and Caius College, and Cambridge, he held posts at Cambridge (ca. 1924–1966), Gonville and Caius College (1963), and the Needham Research Institute (ca. 1976–1990).

Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John Niemeyer Findlay, and held an associate professorship at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007).

Joseph Ratzinger was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Munich and Ducal Georgianum, later holding academic posts at Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen, and Regensburg between 1958 and 1977.

Joseph Rock worked in linguistics, Sinology, and history. He held positions at Mid-Pacific Institute (1908), University of Hawaiʻi (1908–1920), the USDA (ca. 1920–1924), the Army Map Service (1944), and Mills College.

Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at the Jesuit High School of Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (from 1824), INALCO (from 1838), and Société Asiatique (1847, 1852).

Joseph Vendryes was a linguistics scholar. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and under Antoine Meillet. He held major posts at EPHE (ca. 1901–1960), the University of Paris (ca. 1907–1946), and ENS (ca. 1920–1937).
Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He pursued his studies under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (ca. 1788–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ca. 1847–1849).
